NoteTexAccessor::strip_fmt¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::strip_fmt() const

Unwrap Formatting While Keeping Its Text¶

strip_fmt() removes the wrappers \textbf, \textit, \emph, \underline, \texttt, \mathrm, \mathbf, \mathit, and \mathsf, but retains each command’s required argument. It answers a different question from strip_cmds(): formatting is presentation around useful content, so this method promotes the visible body instead of deleting the entire call.

Required groups are brace balanced and nested supported wrappers are processed recursively. Exact command matching leaves longer names unchanged. Escaped commands and commands without a complete required group remain untouched; an incomplete wrapper is not partially unwrapped. Font declaration commands such as \bfseries are outside this narrower contract and remain in the result; strip_fonts() removes those as well.

Whitespace is normalized after unwrapping. The operation is lane-wise, out-of-place, shape preserving, and idempotent. Undefined input propagates and defined non-Text input rejects. Its balanced scan is linear in source plus retained body bytes; recursive memory follows formatting nesting depth.

Example 1: Nested Text And Math Formatting¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \textbf{bold \emph{and nested}} B)",
    R"(\underline{under} \mathrm{x} \texttt{code})",
    R"(\\textbf{escaped} \textbf{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_fmt() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A bold and nested B", "under x code", "\\\\textbf{escaped} \\textbf{unfinished"]

Example 2: Formatting A Matrix Does Not Flatten It¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\mathbf{x})", "plain", R"(\mathsf{y})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_fmt();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_fmt()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["x", "plain"], 
  ["y", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
idempotent=true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_fmt().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_fmt();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip fmt Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip fmt Int64: rejected
